trial_court: Subordinate Judge's Court, Gudivada - Original Petition No. 19 of 1985
case_name: Smt. Kasibhotla Srirani vs Sri Kasibhotla Madhava Rao
facts_of_case: The respondent-husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(1a) and (1b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, alleging that the marriage was against his will and pleasure. The appellant-wife denied all allegations and contended that they lived together till 1980.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party denying a fact to prove that fact.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, we cannot expect any documentary evidence to be produced by the wife showing that Sreemantham function has been performed at the respondent's sister's house.
cited_cases: Smt. Kasibhotla Srirani vs Sri Kasibhotla Madhava Rao, (1993)

legal_principles.principle: The possibility of a fact cannot be ruled out solely based on the absence of evidence.
legal_principles.held: The possibility of the husband taking his wife to the doctor for having consultation with regard to the termination of the pregnancy and he having taken sufficient care cannot be ruled out.
cited_cases: Smt. Kasibhotla Srirani vs Sri Kasibhotla Madhava Rao, (1993)

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decree dissolving the marriage between the parties was set aside, and the appeal was allowed.
